subject: Literacy
title: Clapping the beats in names
objectives: Children will clap the beats in their name.
Children will clap the beats in simple words.
content: Clapping the beats in names, in food and animal names, and sorting words by one, two or three beats.
teachingActivities: Say each word in a steady rhythm and clap once for each beat; start with children’s own names; use two hands or a drum; never ask children to count beats yet, only to clap them.
learnerActivities: Clap the beats in their name and in simple words and match a word to one, two or three claps with support.
resources: Picture cards of a cat, a banana, an elephant and a mango
assessment: Observe whether each child claps the beats in their own name and matches a word to a number of claps with support.
expectedOutcomes: Claps the beats in their own name.
Matches a word to the number of claps with support.

lessons.title: Clap my name
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will clap the beats in their own name.
successCriteria: Claps once for each beat of their name
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can copy a short beat and notice when words sound the same at the end.
lessons.starter: Say a child’s name slowly and clap each beat, for example "A-de-sua" with three claps. Ask "Can we clap your name?"
teacherActivities: Say your own name and clap each beat. Say "Clap with me".
Say one child’s name slowly and clap each beat with the group.
Go round the circle and clap each child’s name.
Play the drum for each name instead of clapping.
learnerActivities: Children clap with you.
Children clap the beats of the name together.
Child claps their own name with support.
Child taps the drum for the beats.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say your own name and clap each beat. Say "Clap with me". Children: Children clap with you.
Step 2. Teacher: Say one child’s name slowly and clap each beat with the group. Children: Children clap the beats of the name together.
Step 3. Teacher: Go round the circle and clap each child’s name. Children: Child claps their own name with support.
Step 4. Teacher: Play the drum for each name instead of clapping. Children: Child taps the drum for the beats.

practical.title: Name claps
steps: Say a name and clap its beats together.
Go round until every child has a turn.
practical.safety: Keep clapping gentle so it does not hurt hands. Include every child’s name and say each correctly.

differentiation.support: Clap the child’s hands for them and say each beat of the name.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to clap a friend’s name.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many claps?
questions.expected: Child shows claps; counting is not required.

expectedOutcomes: Claps the beats in their own name with support
lessons.conclusion: Clap everyone’s name together in one big clap.
lessons.homeConnection: Clap the names of family members at home and say the name as you clap.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "clap the beats in their own name" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Clap your name, clap your name, clap, clap, clap.

lessons.title: Clap food and animals
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will clap the beats in the names of foods and animals.
successCriteria: Claps the beats of a food or animal name
Says the word as they clap
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can copy a short beat and notice when words sound the same at the end.
resources: Picture cards: cat, banana, mango, elephant
lessons.starter: Show the cat card, say "cat" and clap once. Show the banana card, say "ba-na-na" and clap three times.
teacherActivities: Show a picture, say the word slowly and clap each beat.
Show another picture and wait for children to clap before you do.
Play the drum for each word.
Let each child choose a card and lead the clapping.
learnerActivities: Children say and clap each beat.
Children clap the beats on their own.
Children tap or clap along.
Child chooses and the group claps.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a picture, say the word slowly and clap each beat. Children: Children say and clap each beat.
Step 2. Teacher: Show another picture and wait for children to clap before you do. Children: Children clap the beats on their own.
Step 3. Teacher: Play the drum for each word. Children: Children tap or clap along.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a card and lead the clapping. Children: Child chooses and the group claps.

practical.title: Word claps
steps: Place four picture cards face up.
Each child picks one and says the word.
The group claps the beats and says the word again.
practical.safety: Use large cards and keep clapping gentle. Make sure every child has a turn.

differentiation.support: Clap the child’s hands for each beat.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a word with three claps.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says the word as they clap
lessons.conclusion: Clap a favourite word together and say goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Clap the names of foods at mealtimes, such as "rice" and "ba-na-na".
teacherReflection: Which children could show "clap the beats in the names of foods and animals" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: One, two or three claps
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will match a word to one, two or three claps.
successCriteria: Points to the right clap card
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can copy a short beat and notice when words sound the same at the end.
resources: Three baskets labelled one, two and three claps
lessons.starter: Show three baskets with one, two and three hands on them. Say "Some words have one clap, some have two, some have three."
teacherActivities: Show the cat card, clap once and put it in the one-clap basket.
Show the mango card, clap twice and put it in the two-clap basket.
Show the banana card, clap three times and put it in the three-clap basket.
Let each child pick a card, clap and choose a basket.
learnerActivities: Children clap once and watch.
Children clap twice.
Children clap three times.
Child claps and places the card.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the cat card, clap once and put it in the one-clap basket. Children: Children clap once and watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Show the mango card, clap twice and put it in the two-clap basket. Children: Children clap twice.
Step 3. Teacher: Show the banana card, clap three times and put it in the three-clap basket. Children: Children clap three times.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child pick a card, clap and choose a basket. Children: Child claps and places the card.

practical.title: Clap sort
steps: Each child picks a card and claps the word.
Place the card in the matching basket.
practical.safety: Use large cards and keep baskets stable. Supervise turn-taking and help any child who is unsure.

differentiation.support: Clap together and ask the child to point to the basket.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose a new word and sort it.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Which basket does banana go in?

expectedOutcomes: Sorts words by number of claps with support
lessons.conclusion: Put the cards back in order and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Clap the beats in names of things at home and say "one", "two" or "three".
teacherReflection: Which children could show "match a word to one, two or three claps" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Clap and move
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will clap and step the beats of names and words.
successCriteria: Steps or taps once for each beat
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can copy a short beat and notice when words sound the same at the end.
lessons.starter: Say "Walk, walk" and step on each word. Say a name and step on each beat.
teacherActivities: Say a name and step one step for each beat.
Play the drum and let children step on each beat.
Say a food name and let the children step its beats.
Let a child choose a word to step.
learnerActivities: Children step with you.
Children walk on the beat.
Child steps the right number of beats.
Child steps and the group joins.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say a name and step one step for each beat. Children: Children step with you.
Step 2. Teacher: Play the drum and let children step on each beat. Children: Children walk on the beat.
Step 3. Teacher: Say a food name and let the children step its beats. Children: Child steps the right number of beats.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child choose a word to step. Children: Child steps and the group joins.

practical.title: Step the beats
steps: Make a line on the floor.
Say a word and step each beat along the line.
Say the word again at the end.
practical.safety: Clear the floor and keep children well apart. Watch that no one runs.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand and step each beat together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead a friend along the line.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many steps in your name?

expectedOutcomes: Steps the beats of words with support
lessons.conclusion: Take a big step and say "All done."
lessons.homeConnection: Walk and clap the names of family members.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "clap and step the beats of names and words" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 2 beats check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child claps beats in names and words.
successCriteria: Claps the beats in their name
Matches a word to a number of claps
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can copy a short beat and notice when words sound the same at the end.
lessons.starter: Clap names together and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: clap names, clap pictures and clap sort.
At each station ask the child to clap a word.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child claps the word.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: clap names, clap pictures and clap sort. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask the child to clap a word. Children: Child claps the word.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Beat stations
practical.safety: Use soft toys and large cards. Supervise each station and keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and clap together.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to clap a friend’s name.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: claps beats in their own name; claps beats in simple words; sorts words by claps with support.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 2
Claps the beats in their own name
lessons.homeConnection: Clap names at home and say them slowly.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child claps beats in names and words" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
